testCases.testName: [Register] Registration form shows every required field
testCases.description: US1-AC1 - form at /auth/register displays full name, email, masked password, phone, the create-account button and the login link.

testCases.testName: [Register] Navigation header shows the brand and all links
testCases.description: US1-AC2 - BookingCare logo plus Home, Doctor, Search links and the Login / Register buttons.

testCases.testName: [Register] An invalid email format does not create an account
testCases.description: US1-AC3 (negative). FINDING: the app renders no inline error. The email field is type=email required, so submission is blocked by native browser validation and no app-level message appears. Asserted as: still on /auth/register and no server error rendered.

testCases.testName: [Register] Submitting an empty form does not create an account
testCases.description: US1-AC3 (negative) - all fields required. Same finding as TC_REG_03: native validation blocks submission, no app-rendered inline error exists.

testCases.testName: [Register] The password field is masked
testCases.description: US1-AC3 - password is displayed as dots.

testCases.testName: [Register] An invalid phone number does not create an account
testCases.description: US1-AC3 (negative) - phone must be a valid format. EXPECTED TO FAIL: the phone input is type=text with no pattern and no required attribute, so the app appears to accept any value. A failure here is a requirements-versus-implementation defect, not a broken test.

testCases.testName: [Register] Valid details create the account and sign the user in
testCases.description: US1-AC4. The redirect target is /bookings/me, not home or login as the document says. An earlier probe reading that showed no redirect was measured before it completed; with a settle it lands on /bookings/me every time.

testCases.testName: [Register] A duplicate email is rejected with an error
testCases.description: US1-AC5. Error copy confirmed by probe: the app returns Vietnamese text, not the document's English example.

testCases.testName: [Register] The login link navigates to the login page
testCases.description: US1-AC6.

testCases.testName: [Login] Login form shows both fields and the register link
testCases.description: US2-AC1 - email-or-username and masked password fields, submit button, register link.

testCases.testName: [Login] Navigation header shows the brand and all links
testCases.description: US2-AC2.

testCases.testName: [Login] Valid credentials authenticate and the session persists
testCases.description: US2-AC3 - the account is created in preconditions, then signed out is not required: this logs in fresh and confirms the session survives a navigation to another page.

testCases.testName: [Login] An incorrect password shows an error and does not redirect
testCases.description: US2-AC4 (negative). Error copy confirmed by probe as English 'Invalid credentials', which differs from the document's example wording.

testCases.testName: [Login] Submitting an empty form is prevented
testCases.description: US2-AC5 (negative) - both fields required. Same native-validation finding as registration: no app-rendered inline error.

testCases.testName: [Login] The password field is masked
testCases.description: US2-AC5, partial. The other half of this criterion - a teal border on focus - is a CSS pseudo-state and is not assertable through the action set; recorded as not automatable rather than faked.

testCases.testName: [Login] The register link navigates to the registration page
testCases.description: US2-AC6.

testCases.testName: [Providers] Provider list shows every required detail per provider
testCases.description: US3-AC1 - requires an authenticated patient. Asserts all six documented attributes are present on the first card: specialty, experience, rating, fee, hospital, location.

testCases.testName: [Providers] Filtering by specialty narrows the list to that specialty
testCases.description: US3-AC2 - specialty option value confirmed by probe (Tim mach). Asserts the first result actually carries the filtered specialty, not merely that the list re-rendered.

testCases.testName: [Providers] The list can be sorted by check-up fee
testCases.description: US3-AC2, partial. LIMITATION: the 40-action set has no relational assertion, so 'ascending by fee' cannot be verified - only that the control accepts the value and a populated list re-renders. Recorded as a framework gap.

testCases.testName: [Providers] The list can be sorted by rating
testCases.description: US3-AC2, partial. Same relational-assertion limitation as TC_PROV_03.

testCases.testName: [Providers] The detail page opens and carries the booking entry point
testCases.description: US3-AC3, PARTIAL. The criterion says the detail page displays available time slots. It does not - probing found no slot element on that page; slots live on /bookings/new, reached through the book-now link. Asserted here: navigation works and the documented provider details plus the booking entry point are present. The missing slot list is recorded as an unmet requirement, not faked with a selector that does not exist.

testCases.testName: [Booking] Booking an available slot confirms it and lists it under My Appointments
testCases.description: US3-AC4 - only available slots are selectable; after booking, the appointment is confirmed and appears in My Appointments.

testCases.testName: [Booking] A slot already taken is no longer offered as available
testCases.description: US3-AC5, APPROXIMATED. The criterion concerns two users racing for one slot; the framework has no multi-session primitive, so this exercises the server-side conflict rule in a single session - take a slot, then confirm the slot list no longer offers it. Genuine concurrency stays uncovered; see the phase report.

testCases.testName: [Quota] A patient can hold more than one appointment on the same day
testCases.description: US4-AC1 - multiple bookings in one day are allowed, with the same or different providers.

testCases.testName: [Quota] A fourth booking on the same day is rejected with the limit message
testCases.description: US4-AC2 and US4-AC4 - the hardest criterion in the document. Books the three permitted appointments, then asserts the fourth is refused, an error is shown, and the count stays at three.

testCases.testName: [Quota] A cancelled appointment does not count toward the daily limit
testCases.description: US4-AC3 - only valid bookings count toward the limit. Fills the quota, cancels one, then books again successfully.

testCases.testName: [Cancel] Each booked appointment offers a cancel control
testCases.description: US5-AC1 - the cancel option is visible in My Appointments for a booked appointment.

testCases.testName: [Cancel] An appointment more than an hour away can be cancelled
testCases.description: US5-AC2, positive half only. The sub-one-hour half is not reachable through the UI, which offers no slot inside the next hour; recorded as partially covered rather than faked.

testCases.testName: [Cancel] Cancelling asks for confirmation before completing
testCases.description: US5-AC3 - confirmation is required before the cancellation is carried out. The cancelled-status copy is not yet confirmed and is marked TODO_EXPECTED_COPY for the locator pass.

testCases.testName: [Cancel] A cancelled slot is released back into availability
testCases.description: US5-AC4 - after cancellation the slot returns to the provider available slots.

testCases.testName: [Cancel] Cancelling inside the one-hour window is refused
testCases.description: US5-AC5 (negative). NOT FULLY AUTOMATABLE: creating an appointment less than an hour away needs a seeding path, and no API contract is available for this app. Covers the observable half only - a booking exists and no cancellation error is shown in the eligible case.
